Independent verification of the in-flight crossnobis slice. R/crossnobis.R was 7 minutes cold; test file 2 minutes, read but not relied on.

CORRECTNESS - exact. Single realization, 3 runs, obs=40, p=5, Toeplitz(0.35) covariance, known precision, contrast on the condition row:

  package crossnobis : 0.329503620772
  base-R oracle      : 0.329503620772   (mean over ordered a != b of d_a K d_b^T / p)
  max|diff|          : 5.55e-17

estimand label is crossvalidated_squared_mahalanobis_contrast. The implementation is the evidence pairing tr[(c c^T) B_a K B_b^T] as intended, and the /features normalization is a deliberate per-channel convention - worth stating in the docs since it differs from an unnormalized squared Mahalanobis.

YOUR MONTE CARLO TEST HAS REAL POWER. I replicated test-crossnobis-known.R:275 exactly in base R and ran a correct and a deliberately broken (non-crossvalidated) estimator through the same configuration:

                       null mean    se        |mean|/se
  correct (CV)         +0.00365     0.00580   0.63
  broken  (not CV)     +0.09791     0.00611   16.03   <- your 4-se gate CATCHES this

  correct, signal arm: |mean - target|/se = 0.25   (target 0.237202)

So the null arm discriminates at a 16-sigma margin against the most likely failure mode. That is exactly what makes this test worth having rather than a formality, and it closes the "no parameter-recovery tests" gap from the original review. expect_true(any(estimates[, "null"] < 0)) is a good addition too - it pins the signed-negative property.

ONE REFINEMENT, cheap while the epic is open

The tolerance is computed from the observed standard error - 4 * sd(estimates)/sqrt(replications) - rather than prespecified. Epic 6 acceptance says "within a prespecified Monte Carlo error". Adaptive tolerance means a defect that inflates VARIANCE without biasing the mean widens the gate along with the noise and passes. The test currently cannot fail for excess variance.

Concrete fix using measured values from your configuration at replications = 120:

  expected se, null arm   ~ 0.0058
  expected se, signal arm ~ 0.0119

Pin those as constants, keep the 4-sigma mean gates against them, and add an upper bound on the observed se (1.5x the expected value is a reasonable starting point). Then the test fails for bias AND for variance inflation, and the criterion is genuinely prespecified as the acceptance wording requires.
